messages:
ash: Heads up — prepping for the satellite deploy in our customer VPCs next week. Need to lock down segmentation and an end-to-end audit flow for any KMS calls coming from the edge pods. Quick Qs below.
priya: +1. Are we treating the satellite as fully air-gapped, or allowed outbound to our control plane over a private link? That changes egress strategy. :thinking_face:
ash: Private-link only. No public egress. Plan is: mTLS to our control plane over customer VPC peering, and optional on-prem HSM integration.
jorge: For network fencing, I propose calico networkpolicy + host firewall defaults. Minimal cross-namespace allowlist. Example we used before:
```
# deny-by-default example
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-all-ingress
spec:
  podSelector: {}
  policyTypes:
  - Ingress
  - Egress
```
But we need explicit rules for KMS proxy and health checks.
sam: We should also enforce node-level iptables for additional defense (local fail-closed rules), and restrict cluster IP ranges so customer can't accidentally route traffic out.
lina: Audit question — where do audit logs land? Customer wants logs in their SIEM and we need a copy for our billing/quality traces. Are we ok forwarding from the satellite to both endpoints over TLS?
ash: Yes, dual-forward is the plan. Logs remain customer-owned but we forward hashed/pseudonymized telemetry to our control plane. Need to confirm retention & PII rules.
audit-bot: Note: per policy, any forwarded audit must be signed and include non-repudiation header. See spec: /internal/policies/audit-forwarding.
priya: KMS integration details: two modes — 1) customer-managed external KMS reachable via private link, or 2) our managed KMS via dedicated customer key in HSM. For (1) we'll call the customer's KMS through a private ENI; for (2) we create short-lived grants scoped to satellite service identity. Which do we default to?
jorge: Default to customer-managed for regulated customers. For our managed option, we need automated grant revocation on incident and key-rotation tooling. Also consider using token-bound sessions with TTL <= 5m.
ash: RBAC changes: need a new role 'satellite-decrypter' with very narrow permissions, tied to SPIFFE identity of pod. No static access keys. Also add an emergency-revoke playbook that removes grants and rotates session certs.
sam: Vulnerability triage: discovered an old glibc CVE on one base image during build scan. Immediate action: push patched image and trigger rolling restart with canary. If we see exploitation indicators, quarantine node and rotate KMS grants.
lina: For incident response, how do we guarantee isolation? Sequence idea: 1) revoke KMS grants; 2) update network policy to blackhole egress for affected namespace; 3) take forensic snapshot; 4) replace workloads. Is that realistic operationally?
jorge: Yes, but we must ensure revocation can happen without access to control plane if control plane is unreachable. Add local enforcement: a watchdog on the satellite that can flip iptables and drop outbound if it detects suspicious behavior.
ash: Edge-case: if control plane is compromised and issues a revoke, customer might see availability impact. We need an SLA decision: availability vs isolation. Add a canary toggle to allow limited decryption for a short TTL if customer opts in.
priya: Small ask: can security provide a minimal audit event set we must emit (DECRYPT_REQUEST, DECRYPT_SUCCESS, GRANT_REVOKE, NETWORK_QUARANTINE)? We'll include those fields for SIEM mapping.
audit-bot: Emitting required events: [DECRYPT_REQUEST, DECRYPT_SUCCESS, GRANT_REVOKE, KEY_ROTATE, QUARANTINE_START, QUARANTINE_END]. All events must include request_id, pod_id, spiffe_id, and sig.
lina: Last operational note — docs + runbook needed before rollout. I'll create a short canary playbook and post in runbooks/satellite-hardening. Can we get reviews from infra + legal for the PII bits?
ash: Thanks — pairing on this tomorrow with priya & jorge. Action items: priya: ENI/private-link design; jorge: networkpolicy templates + local watchdog; sam: patch plan for base images; lina: audit event spec + runbook. :thumbsup:
